propositions: add_comment returns raw ACLI batch mutation envelope (results/successCount/etc) instead of normalized comment resource, causing consumers to misinterpret work-item keys as comment ids

add_comment must normalize its return via _parse_comment_created to distinguish between DC/REST comment resources (pass through), ACLI batch envelopes (wrap as {id: None, acli_envelope: ...}), and unrecognized shapes (raise RuntimeError)
Other acli_cli_ops --json mutation wrappers (create_issue, get_issue, get_comments) normalize or verify their payloads at transport boundary; add_comment is the sole exception that broke the idiom

The latent raw-passthrough hazard in module-level acli.update_issue (workitem edit --json) has no production consumer-reachable risk today because only opaque read-paths consume it and _check_mutation_failure already guards against failure envelopes
